**Estimating the Economic Value of Accelerating Medical Progress Through New Therapies**

## **Introduction**

Understanding the economic value of new therapies is essential for evaluating the impact of accelerating medical progress. This article explores:

- The **average economic value** of a new therapy.
- The **total annual value** based on the average number of new therapies approved each year.
- An estimation of the potential value created by **increasing trial capacity by {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}}**.

![One cure is worth billions. Fifty cures per year is worth more billions. Twelve times more trials is worth so many billions we had to make a chart.](/assets/images/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments-section-introduction-bw-academic.jpg)

## **Average Economic Value of a New Therapy**

The value of a new therapy can be assessed through market performance and societal benefits:

- **Market Valuation:** Research estimates the average value of a successful new drug at **$1.62 billion [@arxiv-2212-07384]**.
- **Development Costs:** Drug development costs range from **$314 million to $4.46 billion [@jama-2820562]** depending on therapeutic area and clinical complexity.

![Average drug is worth 1.6 billion. Cost to make it: anywhere from cheap to bankruptcy. Pharma: high risk, high reward, high body count.](/assets/images/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments-section-average-economi-bw-academic.jpg)

## **Annual Value Based on Average Approvals**

- **FDA Approvals:** The **FDA [@nature-d41573-025-00001-5]** approves around **{{< var current_drug_approvals_per_year >}} new drugs annually**.
- **Total Annual Value:** Multiplying **{{< var current_drug_approvals_per_year >}} approvals** by **$1.62 billion** yields an estimated **$81 billion** in economic value per year.

![Fifty new drugs per year creates 81 billion dollars of value. That's 1.6 billion per drug. Math: sometimes helpful for explaining why people want more drugs.](/assets/images/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments-section-annual-value-ba-bw-academic.jpg)

## **Impact of {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}} More Trial Capacity**

What would happen with {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}} more trial capacity to test treatments simultaneously?

![Currently: 50 new drugs per year. With more trials: 615 new drugs per year. Subtraction is hard but this seems good.](/assets/images/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments-section-impact-of-bw-academic.jpg)

- **Hypothetical Annual Approvals:** {{< var current_drug_approvals_per_year >}} new therapies × {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}} = **{{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}} {{< var current_drug_approvals_per_year >}} new therapies annually**.
- **Projected Economic Value:** This increased capacity could dramatically accelerate cure discovery, though actual approval rates depend on regulatory capacity and market dynamics.

## **Considerations and Context**

- **Market Saturation:** Rapid introduction of therapies could lead to **price competition** and reduced per-drug economic value.
- **Healthcare System Capacity:** The healthcare infrastructure would need **substantial scaling** to manage increased development and distribution.
- **Societal Benefits:** Beyond direct economic value, accelerated medical progress could lead to **improved health outcomes**, **increased productivity**, and **reduced long-term healthcare costs**.

![Faster cures need three things: money that makes sense, hospitals that work, and everyone not dying. Triangle: the strongest shape in geometry and healthcare policy.](/assets/images/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments-section-considerations-and-context-bw-academic.jpg)

## **Conclusion**

Increasing trial capacity by {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}} through lower-cost decentralized trials (RECOVERY: {{< var recovery_trial_cost_per_patient >}}/patient vs {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}} traditional) enables testing far more treatments at the same time. Market dynamics and system capacities matter, but the basic arithmetic is hard to argue with: spend less per trial, run more trials, find more treatments. Your species has been doing the opposite of this for 60 years, which takes a kind of determination that is almost admirable.

![Old trials: 41,000 dollars per patient. New trials: 500 dollars per patient. Savings: enough to run twelve times more trials, or one very expensive yacht.](/assets/images/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments/economic-value-of-accelerated-treatments-section-conclusion-bw-academic.jpg)
